note: Both sets are highly accurate and faithful to the text, extracting the same core technical specifications (temperature range, strain relationship, CNC details, counts). Set B is slightly better because it explicitly extracts the material (ABS) as a separate attribute in addition to the manufacturing method, providing more granular engineering data. Set B also binds quantity attributes more directly to the components (louvers, rods) rather than the assembly, which is slightly more precise. Set A has slightly more complete quotes in a couple of instances, but the additional correct claim in B makes it more comprehensive.
